signals.name: bit_cnt_q
signals.note: M.1 Path B (§Phase 11): Yosys's flatten + async2sync chain strips the symbol from the state line. The `bit_cnt_q` name appears on a uext alias (NID 47) but Pass 2 attached `bit_cnt_d` first due to line order. `drives: bit_cnt_q` tells mununu's resolver to BFS backward from any node carrying that symbol — picking up the underlying state cell directly. 4-bit counter [0..11] tracking remaining UART frame bits (0 = idle, 10/11 = start of word transmission depending on parity_enable). Bounded at 11 — the max value the design writes (parity_enable=1).

signals.name: baud_div_q
signals.note: M.1: 4-bit baud-rate divider counter [0..15]. Increments on tick_baud_x16; rollover at 16 generates tick_baud_q (the per-bit baud strobe).

signals.name: sreg_q
signals.note: M.1 Path B (§Phase 11): same Yosys-symbol-stripping issue as bit_cnt_q. `drives: sreg_q` routes the resolver to the 11-bit shift-register state cell (NID 53 in current BTOR2) via the uext alias on NID 71. 11-bit shift register holding the frame data. Pinned to reset value (11'h7ff) so the abstract state space stays within the bit-blast cap (2^20). The properties we verify reference `idle` and bit_cnt_q only — sreg_q's value is irrelevant to those. Discover-based widening would push total state bits past 20 (4+4+11+1+1 = 21 > 20); the user can promote sreg_q to bit_blast or discover after R.2.5 predicate-cube lift ships (which doesn't have the MAX_STATE_BITS cap).

signals.name: tx_q
signals.note: M.1 Path B (§Phase 11): the state cell is anonymous in BTOR2; the symbol `tx` only appears as the output port name. `drives: tx` routes the resolver via the output→state alias (1-hop ITE in NID 21). 1-bit serial output register. Boolean abstraction.

signals.name: tick_baud_q
signals.note: M.1: per-bit baud strobe (true for one clock cycle every 16 tick_baud_x16 pulses).

inputs.name: wr_data
inputs.note: M.1: 8-bit payload byte; not relevant to the FSM-state safety property. Ignored to keep the input space tractable.

properties.description: M.1 reachability safety: from every reachable state, the UART can eventually re-enter idle (`bit_cnt_q == 0` while `tx_enable`). Exercises the KMTS lifter on a counter-driven FSM-style design without typedef enums; the verdict's polarity matches what an engineer would expect for a well-formed UART transmitter.
M.1 safety: when `tx_enable` is low, the transmitter reports `idle` on the next cycle (because `bit_cnt_d = 4'h0` in the always_comb). Exercises temporal-modal evaluation.
